selection.name: Alertmanager
selection.role: Provisional routing engine, assessed at v0.34.1. Accept alerts generated by the metrics and logs systems, then deduplicate, group, silence, inhibit and route them to ntfy. Its documented amtool CLI provides an interface agent sessions can call.

basis.shows: Direct capability fit: receiver routing, deduplication, grouping, silencing and inhibition. Documents Docker installation and amtool commands. The install command applies the observed release tag to the documented Docker example; receiver configuration and persistent storage still need configuration.
Version-pinned correctness evidence includes TestDedupStageNeedsUpdate and TestDedupStage, covering notification decisions for firing and resolved alert sets and repeat intervals.
TestLogSnapshot checks notification-log snapshot storage and restoration, directly relevant to retaining deduplication state.
Tests cover silence matching, expiry and snapshot restoration. These support the required silence semantics, without establishing end-to-end restart delivery on WSL2.
The latest sampled default-branch Test job completed SUCCESS on 2026-09-29 at commit 61ba43d505ca5867ddfee77fc7a64ee80b114454. This is an upstream CI result, not a target-host comparison.

Latest stable release v0.34.1 was published 2026-09-17, within 90 days. Assets include Linux amd64 and native Darwin arm64 binaries. Release notes identify inhibition fixes relevant to correct muting.
Latest default-branch commit was 2026-09-29, within the frozen maintenance window.
Repository is unarchived. GitHub identifies Apache-2.0 as its license; license was not used as a ranking criterion.

selection.name: ntfy
selection.role: Device-delivery endpoint, assessed at v2.28.0. Its built-in Alertmanager template renders grouped firing and resolved webhook payloads for subscribers. Configure an on-disk message cache for restart durability; grouping and silencing belong to Alertmanager.

basis.shows: Documents built-in Alertmanager and Grafana webhook templates, selected using a template header or query parameter. This gives the proposed pair an upstream-supported integration without a custom adapter.
The stable-tag template explicitly handles firing and resolved status and renders the alerts in the incoming group.

Documents persistent SQLite/PostgreSQL message caching, subscriber replay and Web Push configuration. Default caching is in memory and does not survive restart. Instant iOS delivery requires an APNS-connected upstream; self-hosting therefore does not imply fully local instant delivery on every device.

Version-pinned tests cover publishing, polling, cursor-based cached retrieval and JSON message templating. They provide relevant correctness evidence, but not measured notification delivery to the user's devices.
The latest sampled default-branch test job completed SUCCESS on 2026-09-29 at commit 1e6305ccecc0af15b13d239c3281543bea27b960.
Latest stable release v2.28.0 was published 2026-08-27, within 90 days. Linux amd64 packages and a macOS CLI tarball are published.

Documents the Linux package installation used above. Official macOS support covers publish/subscribe CLI use; the server is not officially supported on macOS. The macOS arm64 binary architecture was not independently inspected.
Latest default-branch commit was 2026-09-29, within the frozen maintenance window.
Repository is unarchived and describes phone/desktop notification delivery through HTTP. The selected path can be self-hosted without purchasing a service.

layers.deciding_comparison: The selected pair is a provisional preference based on documented fit and relevant upstream correctness evidence, not a measured winner. On a clean WSL2 Ubuntu x86_64 host, compare Alertmanager v0.34.1 plus ntfy v2.28.0 against Grafana Alerting v13.2.3 plus the same ntfy endpoint. Replay identical firing/resolved metric-and-log fixtures with matched grouping labels, repeat intervals and silence schedules. Measure missing transitions, unintended duplicates, group contents, silence correctness and delivery latency on the Windows browser, actual phones and a macOS arm64 subscriber. Repeat after subscriber disconnection, graceful service restart and forced termination with persistent state configured. Prefer the arm with fewer missing transitions, then fewer unintended duplicates and correct silence/state restoration. No recorded comparison in the packet resolves this.
evidence_gaps: No supplied head-to-head ran the competing repositories, and no target-host delivery comparison was performed here. Upstream tests and CI establish sampled correctness, not comparative device-delivery reliability.

The packet does not identify the metrics/logs systems or their alert interface. Alertmanager consumes generated alerts rather than evaluating arbitrary raw metrics and logs; source compatibility remains an installation prerequisite.

Linux amd64 release availability supports architectural fit for WSL2, but WSL2 execution, service startup, Windows notification visibility and restart behavior were not measured. The layer does not call for GPU computation; no RTX 4090 benchmark is relevant to this selection.

ntfy's durable cache is opt-in. Its official macOS support is CLI-only, and instant iOS delivery uses an upstream push connection. Device types and acceptable external push dependencies were not specified.

Maintenance snapshot: 2026-10-02T03:26:55Z, corresponding to 2026-10-01 in the supplied timezone. All 11 repository endpoints reported unarchived repositories, all latest default-branch commits fell within 90 days, and recent issue or PR updates were observed for every candidate. Release dates are reported per candidate. The GraphQL activity sample does not establish issue-response or resolution rates: https://api.github.com/graphql.

CI evidence was sampled at the latest default-branch heads and kept separate from version-pinned test-source inspection. Grafana's sampled head rollup was successful without a relevant alert-delivery test among the first 20 contexts; Nightingale had no rollup; Gotify had mixed job outcomes. None of these observations proves general test coverage or comparative reliability.
